description: Lamb Ouzi is a celebrated Middle Eastern dish featuring tender, spiced lamb often served over aromatic rice with nuts and peas. This recipe offers a quicker preparation for a family-style Ouzi, delivering rich flavors without the extensive slow-roasting time. It is a hearty and flavorful meal perfect for gatherings or a special weeknight dinner.

instructions.title: Prepare and Sear the Lamb
instructions.text: Pat the lamb cubes dry and season them generously with 1 tablespoon of the Ouzi spice blend, salt, and black pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon of oil or ghee in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the lamb in batches and sear until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove the lamb and set aside.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil or ghee to the same pot. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn the garlic.

instructions.title: Cook the Spiced Rice
instructions.text: Drain the soaked basmati rice and add it to the pot with the onions and garlic. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon of Ouzi spice blend and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, to lightly toast the rice and infuse it with the spices.

instructions.title: Simmer the Ouzi
instructions.text: Return the seared lamb to the pot with the rice. Pour in the hot chicken or lamb broth and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the rice is cooked through and most of the liquid has been absorbed. The lamb should be tender.

instructions.title: Add Peas and Nuts
instructions.text: Once the rice is cooked, gently stir in the thawed frozen peas. Fluff the rice with a fork. In a separate small pan, quickly toast the pine nuts and slivered almonds over medium heat until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes. Be careful as they can burn quickly.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Transfer the Lamb Ouzi to a large serving platter. Garnish generously with the toasted pine nuts, slivered almonds, and fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot as a complete and satisfying Middle Eastern meal. A side of plain yogurt or a simple salad pairs wonderfully.

tips: For an extra layer of flavor, brown the lamb bones (if using a bone-in cut) and use them to make your own lamb broth.
The Ouzi spice blend is key; adjust the ratios of allspice, cinnamon, and cardamom to your personal preference.
For best results, let the Ouzi rest covered for 5-10 minutes after cooking to allow the flavors to meld and the rice to fully absorb any remaining moisture.
article:
Unveiling the majestic centerpiece of Middle Eastern feasting, Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted is more than just a meal; it's a grand culinary experience designed to impress and delight. Imagine a whole leg of lamb, so incredibly tender it practically melts off the bone, infused with a symphony of aromatic spices, and served atop a bed of fragrant, fluffy basmati rice studded with toasted nuts and sweet peas. This isn't just a dinner; it's a celebration, a testament to the rich flavors and generous hospitality that define Middle Eastern cuisine. While the idea of slow-roasting a whole lamb might sound daunting, this comprehensive guide will break down every step, ensuring you master this show-stopping dish. Prepare to embark on a culinary journey that will leave your guests in awe and your taste buds singing. This authentic Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted is an unforgettable addition to your repertoire of Middle Eastern dinner recipes.

## What is Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted?

Lamb Ouzi, or Qoozi, is a renowned Middle Eastern festive dish, traditionally served at special occasions, weddings, and large family gatherings. While there are variations across the region – some involving lamb cooked inside a pastry shell – the "whole slow roasted" version truly showcases the lamb's inherent richness and tenderness. At its heart, Ouzi combines succulent, spice-infused lamb with a richly flavored rice pilaf, often incorporating ground meat, peas, and a generous scattering of toasted nuts like pine nuts, almonds, or cashews.

The magic of the "whole slow roasted" method lies in its ability to transform tougher cuts of lamb into unbelievably tender, fall-apart meat. By cooking the lamb at a low temperature for several hours, the connective tissues gradually break down, rendering the meat incredibly moist and flavorful. This slow process also allows the intricate blend of Middle Eastern spices to deeply penetrate the meat, creating a complex aroma and taste that is simply irresistible. This method not only guarantees an exquisite flavor profile but also ensures the lamb is incredibly easy to carve or even pull apart, making it a truly magnificent centerpiece for any gathering. It’s a quintessential example of impressive Middle Eastern Dinner Recipes.

## Ingredients You Need for Lamb Ouzi

Crafting the perfect Lamb Ouzi requires a selection of fresh, high-quality ingredients. Here's what you'll need to create this magnificent Lamb Ouzi Recipe:

For the Lamb:
*   1 whole bone-in lamb leg or shoulder (approx. 5-7 lbs / 2.5-3.5 kg)
*   4-5 cloves garlic, minced
*   1/4 cup olive oil
*   2 tablespoons lemon juice
*   2 tablespoons Middle Eastern seven-spice blend
*   1 tablespoon ground cinnamon
*   1 teaspoon ground cardamom
*   1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg
*   1 teaspoon black pepper
*   2 teaspoons salt
*   1 large onion, quartered
*   2 cups lamb or chicken broth

For the Aromatic Rice:
*   3 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
*   2 tablespoons olive oil or ghee
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   2 cloves garlic, minced
*   1 cup frozen peas
*   1/2 cup toasted pine nuts
*   1/2 cup toasted slivered almonds
*   1/2 lb ground lamb or beef (optional, for richer rice)
*   1 tablespoon Middle Eastern seven-spice blend
*   1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
*   1/2 teaspoon ground cardamom
*   1/4 teaspoon ground cloves
*   4 cups lamb or chicken broth
*   Salt and black pepper to taste

Garnish:
*   Fresh parsley, chopped
*   Extra toasted nuts

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Lamb Ouzi

Follow this detailed Lamb Ouzi Recipe to create a show-stopping dish that will impress everyone at your table.

1.  **Prepare the Lamb:** Pat the lamb leg dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, score the fatty side of the lamb in a diamond pattern, about 1/2 inch deep. In a small bowl, combine minced garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, seven-spice blend, cinnamon, cardamom, nutmeg, black pepper, and salt to form a paste. Generously rub this spice paste all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into the scored cuts. For best results, place the lamb in a large roasting pan, cover, and refrigerate to marinate for at least 4 hours, or ideally overnight.

2.  **Slow Roast the Lamb:** Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C). Place the marinated lamb in a sturdy roasting pan. Add the quartered onion and 2 cups of lamb or chicken broth to the bottom of the pan. Cover the roasting pan tightly with aluminum foil, ensuring no steam can escape. Roast for 4-5 hours, or until the lamb is incredibly tender and easily pulls apart with a fork. For the last 30-45 minutes, remove the foil and increase the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C) to allow the lamb to brown and develop a beautiful crust. Once cooked, remove the lamb from the oven, transfer it to a cutting board, cover loosely with foil, and let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes. This resting period is crucial for the juices to redistribute, ensuring moist, flavorful meat.

3.  **Prepare the Aromatic Rice:** While the lamb is resting, prepare the rice. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat olive oil or ghee over medium heat. If using ground lamb, add it and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned. Drain any excess fat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the rinsed and soaked basmati rice, seven-spice, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves. Stir well to coat the rice with the spices. Pour in the 4 cups of lamb or chicken broth, season with salt and pepper, and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is tender.

4.  **Finish the Rice:** Once the rice is cooked, remove it from the heat and let it sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Stir in the frozen peas (their residual heat will cook them) and most of the toasted pine nuts and almonds, reserving some for garnish.

5.  **Assemble and Serve:** On a large serving platter, spoon out the aromatic rice, forming a generous bed. Carve or shred the slow-roasted lamb and arrange it beautifully over the rice. Drizzle with any pan juices from the roasting pan (skim off excess fat first). Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley and the reserved toasted nuts. Serve immediately and watch your guests marvel at this incredible Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted.

## Pro Tips for the Best Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

Achieving perfection with your Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted involves a few key techniques:

*   **Marinate Liberally and Long:** Don't skimp on marinating time. The longer the lamb sits in the spice rub (ideally 24 hours), the deeper the flavors will penetrate, resulting in a more aromatic and delicious roast.
*   **The Power of Low and Slow:** Resist the urge to rush the roasting process. The low oven temperature and extended cooking time are essential for breaking down the tough fibers in the lamb, yielding that signature fall-off-the-bone tenderness.
*   **Resting is Non-Negotiable:** After roasting, always rest the lamb. This allows the muscle fibers to relax and reabsorb the juices, ensuring a moist and succulent result. Skip this step, and your lamb might be dry.
*   **Quality Spices Matter:** Use fresh, good-quality Middle Eastern spices. Old, stale spices lose their potency and won't impart the vibrant flavors necessary for an authentic Ouzi.
*   **Perfectly Cooked Rice:** Avoid overcooking the basmati rice. It should be fluffy and separate, not mushy. Rinsing and soaking the rice helps achieve this texture.
*   **Toast Your Nuts:** Toasting pine nuts and almonds (either in a dry pan or a low oven) before adding them to the rice or using as a garnish significantly enhances their flavor and aroma.

## Serving Suggestions for Lamb Ouzi

Lamb Ouzi is a complete meal in itself, but it truly shines when presented as part of a larger Middle Eastern Dinner Recipes spread. Traditionally, it's served on a grand platter, with the shredded lamb majestically placed atop the fragrant rice.

Complement this magnificent dish with simple yet refreshing sides:
*   **Yogurt-Cucumber Salad:** A cooling salad like Tzatziki or a simple plain yogurt mixed with grated cucumber, garlic, and mint provides a lovely contrast to the richness of the lamb.
*   **Simple Green Salad:** A light salad with a lemon-tahini dressing can add freshness.
*   **Extra Nuts and Herbs:** Offer additional toasted nuts and fresh parsley for guests to sprinkle on their portions.
*   **Pan Juices:** Defat any pan juices from the lamb roasting pan and serve them alongside as a natural gravy.

## Variations and Substitutions for Lamb Ouzi

While this Lamb Ouzi Recipe is designed for a whole slow-roasted leg, you can adapt it to suit your needs and preferences:

*   **Meat Cuts:** If a whole leg is too much, you can use a bone-in lamb shoulder or even large lamb shanks. Adjust cooking time accordingly; shanks will cook faster. Beef roast can be used, though it won't be traditional Ouzi.
*   **Rice Fillings:** For an even richer rice, brown 1/2 lb of ground lamb or beef with the onions before adding the rice and broth. You can also experiment with different nuts or dried fruits like apricots or raisins for a touch of sweetness.
*   **Spice Adjustments:** Feel free to tweak the spice blend. Some recipes incorporate dried lime (loomi) for a unique tangy note.
*   **Individual Portions:** While this article focuses on the whole roast, Ouzi is sometimes served by wrapping individual portions of rice and shredded lamb in thin filo pastry (phyllo dough) and baking until golden. This makes for a stunning individual presentation.

Embarking on the journey of making Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted is a rewarding experience that culminates in an unforgettable feast. This impressive Middle Eastern dinner recipe, with its tender, spiced lamb and aromatic rice, promises to be the star of any gathering. It’s a dish that embodies warmth, generosity, and the rich culinary heritage of the Middle East, inviting everyone to gather, share, and savor every delicious bite.
